answer.rationale: p99 write-path latency is climbing under heavy, peak settlement load; the security patch cannot be reverted, ruling out rollback. Adding capacity is slow and may not relieve a latency surge already in progress, and regional failover risks failing over active customer writes during peak. The most defensible single intervention is enabling/expanding a circuit breaker on the payments write dependency: memory_b4 shows this exact pattern previously contained a partner outage by failing fast on the dependency while preserving the rest of the checkout path. That experience directly supports using the same mechanism here to shed latency-inducing calls and protect sustained availability of the core write path. I will roll it out as a small, guarded change and verify impact before broadening scope.
